sourceDescription: 50-item assessment supplied by the user; original practice wording and corrected explanations. Source text itself is not republished.

gpu.title: Microsoft: GPU data in Task Manager

items.title: Application, OS and driver roles
items.sourceItem: User-supplied front-of-book assessment, item 1; rewritten after correction review
items.fact: An application performs the user-facing task; the OS supplies shared services.
items.trap: Drivers connect the OS to hardware; a filesystem organizes stored data.
items.transfer: Change the symptom to missing device support. Which layer should you investigate?
items.recall: Spreadsheet application

items.title: ChromeOS can work offline
items.sourceItem: User-supplied front-of-book assessment, item 2; rewritten after correction review
items.fact: ChromeOS supports offline-capable applications and prepared local data.
items.trap: Offline availability depends on the app and file configuration; Linux has roles beyond desktops.
items.transfer: Identify what must be prepared before taking a cloud document offline.
items.recall: Offline-capable apps and locally available files can work without an active connection

items.title: Source code and compilation
items.sourceItem: User-supplied front-of-book assessment, item 3; rewritten after correction review
items.fact: Source code is input to compilation in this workflow.
items.trap: Calling source code precompiled machine instructions confuses the input with the output.
items.transfer: How does an interpreted script differ from this simplified compiled workflow?
items.recall: Source code

items.title: Mobile operating systems
items.sourceItem: User-supplied front-of-book assessment, item 4; rewritten after correction review
items.fact: Android is a mobile operating system in the smartphone scenario.
items.trap: An OS category does not imply that every application or feature requires cloud access.
items.transfer: Contrast the support needs of a mobile OS with a server workload.
items.recall: Mobile operating system

items.title: Preview versus production releases
items.sourceItem: User-supplied front-of-book assessment, item 5; rewritten after correction review
items.fact: Windows Insider distributes preview builds for evaluation.
items.trap: Preview channels and eligibility change; use current guidance and keep a recovery plan instead of old Windows servicing names.
items.transfer: Would the same risk be appropriate for a critical production workstation? Explain.
items.recall: Windows Insider Program

items.title: Prepare an image before capture
items.sourceItem: User-supplied front-of-book assessment, item 6; rewritten after correction review
items.fact: Sysprep /generalize prepares a reference installation by removing machine-specific information.
items.trap: A WIM is an image format; capture and deployment are separate operations. Use supported imaging procedures.
items.transfer: Place generalization, offline capture and target deployment in order.
items.recall: Sysprep with /generalize

items.title: Boot configuration data
items.sourceItem: User-supplied front-of-book assessment, item 7; rewritten after correction review
items.fact: BCD holds Windows boot configuration used by the boot manager.
items.trap: UEFI and legacy boot components differ; hibernation resume is not the same as a normal OS boot.
items.transfer: Which evidence would distinguish a missing boot entry from an application startup failure?
items.recall: Boot Configuration Data (BCD) store

items.title: Static IP configuration paths
items.sourceItem: User-supplied front-of-book assessment, item 8; rewritten after correction review
items.fact: Windows network Settings can configure manual IP assignment for an adapter.
items.trap: Adapter properties reached through Control Panel can also configure IP; a question must constrain the path if only one answer is intended.
items.transfer: List the IP, mask/prefix, gateway and DNS information you would verify after the change.
items.recall: Settings → Network & internet → the adapter’s IP settings

items.title: Fragmentation is still possible
items.sourceItem: User-supplied front-of-book assessment, item 9; rewritten after correction review
items.fact: ext4 uses allocation strategies to improve data locality and reduce fragmentation.
items.trap: These mechanisms are not a guarantee of automatic, continuous defragmentation.
items.transfer: Explain why avoiding fragmentation is different from guaranteeing contiguous storage.
items.recall: Its allocation strategies reduce fragmentation, but fragmentation can still occur

items.title: Update macOS through Software Update
items.sourceItem: User-supplied front-of-book assessment, item 10; rewritten after correction review
items.fact: Current macOS updates are offered through Software Update in System Settings.
items.trap: App Store app updates are a different task; older macOS versions may use different paths.
items.transfer: What compatibility and backup checks belong before a major upgrade?
items.recall: System Settings → General → Software Update

items.title: Finder manages files
items.sourceItem: User-supplied front-of-book assessment, item 11; rewritten after correction review
items.fact: Finder is the standard macOS file-browsing interface.
items.trap: Browsing a file is different from installing an OS update or managing firmware.
items.transfer: Choose a different macOS tool to inspect a process that consumes excessive CPU.
items.recall: Finder

items.title: Search names versus contents
items.sourceItem: User-supplied front-of-book assessment, item 12; rewritten after correction review
items.fact: grep -r searches matching text through files recursively.
items.trap: find traverses directories by default; -name matches entry names rather than searching each file’s contents.
items.transfer: Change the requirement to finding files whose names end in .log. Which tool and predicate fit?
items.recall: grep -r timeout ./logs

items.title: Password guessing
items.sourceItem: User-supplied front-of-book assessment, item 13; rewritten after correction review
items.fact: Repeated candidate-password attempts are evidence of password guessing.
items.trap: The log does not by itself prove successful access. Investigate outcomes and apply approved authentication protections.
items.transfer: What additional evidence would establish that an account was compromised?
items.recall: Password guessing

items.title: Biometrics and authentication factors
items.sourceItem: User-supplied front-of-book assessment, item 14; rewritten after correction review
items.fact: A fingerprint is a biometric characteristic.
items.trap: A PIN and password are both knowledge factors; a smart card/token is possession, not a biological characteristic.
items.transfer: Why do two passwords not automatically provide two different authentication factors?
items.recall: Fingerprint recognition

items.title: Rootkit concealment
items.sourceItem: User-supplied front-of-book assessment, item 15; rewritten after correction review
items.fact: A rootkit is associated with concealed malicious presence or control.
items.trap: A symptom is a clue, not proof; follow the incident workflow and use trusted inspection/recovery methods.
items.transfer: Why might recovery from trusted media be needed when the running OS cannot be trusted?
items.recall: Rootkit

items.title: Physical security boundaries
items.sourceItem: User-supplied front-of-book assessment, item 16; rewritten after correction review
items.fact: A fence creates a physical perimeter control.
items.trap: Physical controls complement authentication and monitoring; a fence alone does not grant or verify digital access.
items.transfer: What control would verify identity at the building entrance?
items.recall: A perimeter fence

items.title: Metal-detector limits
items.sourceItem: User-supplied front-of-book assessment, item 17; rewritten after correction review
items.fact: A metal detector detects metal under its operating conditions.
items.trap: It is not a universal weapon detector or a substitute for identity checks.
items.transfer: Name a risk this physical control does not address.
items.recall: It can detect relevant metal objects within its operating limits

items.title: Sync is not independent backup
items.sourceItem: User-supplied front-of-book assessment, item 18; rewritten after correction review
items.fact: Synchronization coordinates selected data and may propagate deletion.
items.trap: Recoverability depends on retention, versioning and backup configuration, not merely having two synced devices.
items.transfer: How would you verify that a deleted test file can actually be recovered?
items.recall: Synchronization can propagate deletions, so recovery needs separate retention/version or backup controls

items.title: Firewall rules and tamper protection
items.sourceItem: User-supplied front-of-book assessment, item 19; rewritten after correction review
items.fact: Advanced Security manages scoped firewall rules.
items.trap: Defender Tamper Protection restricts unauthorized security-setting changes; it is not the tool for authoring firewall rules.
items.transfer: Which profile, program, source and port restrictions should you verify before enabling a rule?
items.recall: Windows Defender Firewall with Advanced Security

items.title: Workstation hardening
items.sourceItem: User-supplied front-of-book assessment, item 20; rewritten after correction review
items.fact: Hardening combines maintained software with restricted access and appropriate authentication.
items.trap: Renaming an account alone does not prevent compromise; disabling protective controls weakens the baseline.
items.transfer: How would you verify that normal users can work without unnecessary administrator rights?
items.recall: Supported updates, least privilege, strong authentication and controlled administrative access

items.title: File encryption versus volume encryption
items.sourceItem: User-supplied front-of-book assessment, item 21; rewritten after correction review
items.fact: EFS provides file-level encryption on supported Windows/NTFS configurations.
items.trap: Do not rule out BitLocker solely because a TPM is absent: supported non-TPM configurations exist. Plan recovery of encryption credentials.
items.transfer: When would volume-level BitLocker be the better match than EFS?
items.recall: Encrypting File System (EFS)

items.title: Verify folder-backup configuration
items.sourceItem: User-supplied front-of-book assessment, item 22; rewritten after correction review
items.fact: OneDrive folder backup requires the relevant client, account and folder configuration.
items.trap: A Microsoft account alone is not evidence that every file or folder is protected.
items.transfer: Create a harmless test file and describe how you would confirm upload and recovery.
items.recall: The OneDrive account, selected folders, backup configuration and sync/backup status

items.title: Built-in GPU performance monitoring
items.sourceItem: User-supplied front-of-book assessment, item 23; rewritten after correction review
items.fact: Task Manager can display GPU data with supported hardware and drivers.
items.trap: Third-party tools may add detail, but they are not always required. GPU support depends on the driver model.
items.transfer: What would you check if the GPU graph is absent?
items.recall: Task Manager

items.title: End malware removal with education
items.sourceItem: User-supplied front-of-book assessment, item 24; rewritten after correction review
items.fact: End-user education helps prevent recurrence after the required remediation and recovery steps.
items.trap: Education is not a substitute for containment, removal, validation or the organization’s incident procedure.
items.transfer: Change the case to an organization-managed device. Who must approve recovery and communication?
items.recall: Educate the end user about avoiding recurrence

items.title: Match Wi-Fi changes to evidence
items.sourceItem: User-supplied front-of-book assessment, item 25; rewritten after correction review
items.fact: An alternative supported band may reduce the measured 2.4 GHz interference.
items.trap: Range, obstructions and coverage still matter; 5 GHz is not a universal cure for disconnections.
items.transfer: What changes if the client is at the edge of coverage rather than near the AP?
items.recall: Move the client to an appropriately configured 5 GHz connection and remeasure

items.title: USB controller-resource troubleshooting
items.sourceItem: User-supplied front-of-book assessment, item 26; rewritten after correction review
items.fact: USB devices can share controller resources even across different physical ports.
items.trap: Check power, bandwidth, controller topology and supported drivers; port generation/color alone does not establish the cause.
items.transfer: What evidence would instead suggest a power-budget problem?
items.recall: Check topology and move a device to a suitable port on a different controller, then retest

items.title: Virtual-machine clock synchronization
items.sourceItem: User-supplied front-of-book assessment, item 27; rewritten after correction review
items.fact: Virtual timekeeping and pause/resume behavior can cause clock drift.
items.trap: The correct time source depends on the configuration; domain members commonly use the domain hierarchy.
items.transfer: Why can an inaccurate clock affect authentication and log correlation?
items.recall: Check supported host/guest time integration and the guest’s configured time hierarchy

items.title: Manage a Windows service
items.sourceItem: User-supplied front-of-book assessment, item 28; rewritten after correction review
items.fact: The Services management console controls supported service operations.
items.trap: Review dependencies and the failure cause; changing startup settings is different from restarting a running service.
items.transfer: What would you record if the service stops again immediately?
items.recall: Services (services.msc), also available through Computer Management

items.title: Battery thermal hazards
items.sourceItem: User-supplied front-of-book assessment, item 29; rewritten after correction review
items.fact: A damaged or overheated lithium-ion battery can present a serious thermal hazard.
items.trap: Follow manufacturer and workplace handling/escalation guidance; do not puncture, charge or improvise a repair.
items.transfer: Which approved channel handles safe isolation and disposal in your workplace?
items.recall: Thermal runaway, fire or related injury risk

items.title: Shutdown evidence versus cause
items.sourceItem: User-supplied front-of-book assessment, item 30; rewritten after correction review
items.fact: Unexpected-shutdown logs are evidence to correlate with other symptoms and records.
items.trap: A shutdown event does not independently identify the root cause.
items.transfer: What additional evidence would support a power, thermal or driver hypothesis?
items.recall: The previous shutdown was unexpected; investigate correlated evidence for the cause

items.title: RDP transport and default port
items.sourceItem: User-supplied front-of-book assessment, item 31; rewritten after correction review
items.fact: Direct RDP commonly uses TCP and UDP port 3389.
items.trap: Gateways and configured ports can change the path; do not assume TCP is its only possible transport.
items.transfer: How does a Remote Desktop Gateway change the externally exposed path?
items.recall: TCP and UDP 3389

items.title: Batch-file comments
items.sourceItem: User-supplied front-of-book assessment, item 32; rewritten after correction review
items.fact: REM records a batch-file comment.
items.trap: Comment syntax depends on the interpreter; PowerShell/Bash and JavaScript examples do not become cmd.exe comments.
items.transfer: Which interpreter and comment syntax would apply to a .ps1 file?
items.recall: REM Explain the next step

items.title: Launch the RDP client
items.sourceItem: User-supplied front-of-book assessment, item 33; rewritten after correction review
items.fact: mstsc launches the Windows Remote Desktop Connection client.
items.trap: Launching a client does not establish authorization, reachability or permission to control the target.
items.transfer: Which target, network and permission checks belong before connecting?
items.recall: mstsc.exe

items.title: Remote-access VPN
items.sourceItem: User-supplied front-of-book assessment, item 34; rewritten after correction review
items.fact: A host-to-site VPN connects an individual remote client to the organization’s network.
items.trap: A VPN does not remove endpoint, authentication or application-authorization requirements.
items.transfer: How would the diagram change for a branch-office site-to-site VPN?
items.recall: Remote-access / host-to-site VPN

items.title: Collaboration tools
items.sourceItem: User-supplied front-of-book assessment, item 35; rewritten after correction review
items.fact: Videoconferencing is the relevant collaboration capability.
items.trap: Platforms such as Teams/Zoom may also support chat, sharing and other features; one label does not exclude the others.
items.transfer: Which meeting, sharing and privacy settings should the organizer verify?
items.recall: Videoconferencing in a suitable collaboration platform

items.title: Verify AI-generated guidance
items.sourceItem: User-supplied front-of-book assessment, item 36; rewritten after correction review
items.fact: AI-generated technical guidance needs independent validation and policy review.
items.trap: Confidence and fluent language do not establish accuracy or permission; protect sensitive data.
items.transfer: How would you test a proposed command using disposable example data?
items.recall: Verify the command, authorization, backup and consequences before considering execution

items.title: Approved ESD controls
items.sourceItem: User-supplied front-of-book assessment, item 37; rewritten after correction review
items.fact: Approved ESD equipment and handling procedures reduce damaging potential differences.
items.trap: Hair restraint can address other hazards, but it does not replace ESD controls. Follow electrical-safety and equipment guidance.
items.transfer: Why must the approved servicing procedure be checked before connecting an ESD strap?
items.recall: Use the approved antistatic wrist strap and connection procedure; Use an approved ESD work surface/mat as directed

items.title: Use the correct driver bit
items.sourceItem: User-supplied front-of-book assessment, item 38; rewritten after correction review
items.fact: Use the matching driver type and size to avoid damaging the fastener or equipment.
items.trap: Torx has a familiar six-lobed form; security variants can require a corresponding special bit.
items.transfer: What should you do when the specified fastener does not match your available tool?
items.recall: The matching Torx bit and size

items.title: Trial licensing and open source
items.sourceItem: User-supplied front-of-book assessment, item 39; rewritten after correction review
items.fact: Shareware commonly offers trial or limited use before purchase.
items.trap: Open-source software can be used commercially under its license; price and licensing rights are separate questions.
items.transfer: Which rights and restrictions would you check before installing software for a business?
items.recall: Shareware / trial software

items.title: ESD strap resistance
items.sourceItem: User-supplied front-of-book assessment, item 40; rewritten after correction review
items.fact: Approved wrist straps commonly include a series safety resistor, often around one megaohm.
items.trap: Use the manufacturer-approved equipment and bonding procedure; this is not a universal instruction for every grounding system.
items.transfer: Explain why a bare improvised wire is not an equivalent substitute.
items.recall: It limits current while providing the intended controlled discharge path

items.title: Choose PPE from the hazard
items.sourceItem: User-supplied front-of-book assessment, item 41; rewritten after correction review
items.fact: PPE and cleaning methods should match the actual hazard and approved procedure.
items.trap: A filtration mask can be appropriate for airborne particles, but it is not a universal answer for every task.
items.transfer: How would your preparation change for damaged batteries or hazardous toner?
items.recall: The task hazards, manufacturer instructions and applicable safety guidance

items.title: Microwave interference scope
items.sourceItem: User-supplied front-of-book assessment, item 42; rewritten after correction review
items.fact: Microwave-related interference can affect 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi.
items.trap: Validate timing, signal and band conditions; this is not a claim that every wireless failure or band has the same cause.
items.transfer: Design a comparison test that changes one relevant condition at a time.
items.recall: Interference affecting the 2.4 GHz connection

items.title: Respect access authorization
items.sourceItem: User-supplied front-of-book assessment, item 43; rewritten after correction review
items.fact: Visible credentials do not grant permission to use another person’s account.
items.trap: The approved contact method may be a call, ticket or other channel; texting is not universally required.
items.transfer: How can an approved support account or supervised session avoid impersonating the user?
items.recall: Use an approved contact/access process and obtain the required authorization

items.title: Report accidental damage
items.sourceItem: User-supplied front-of-book assessment, item 44; rewritten after correction review
items.fact: Honest communication and documented escalation preserve trust and support safe resolution.
items.trap: Do not conceal damage or continue with a component known to be unsafe or faulty.
items.transfer: Which ticket and inventory records should be updated?
items.recall: Disclose the damage promptly and follow the approved resolution/escalation process

items.title: Communicate a changed estimate
items.sourceItem: User-supplied front-of-book assessment, item 45; rewritten after correction review
items.fact: Communicate delays and revised expectations proactively.
items.trap: An estimate is not permission to hide risk or mark unfinished work resolved.
items.transfer: What would you communicate if the next step depends on an uncertain parts delivery?
items.recall: Notify the customer, explain the status and provide a revised realistic estimate

items.title: Ticket intake depends on the workflow
items.sourceItem: User-supplied front-of-book assessment, item 46; rewritten after correction review
items.fact: The correct intake channel follows the organization’s configured and accessible workflow.
items.trap: Email, portals, staff entry and automated alerts have different uses; no one method is universally easiest.
items.transfer: How would you handle a request containing sensitive data in the ticket body?
items.recall: Email the approved support address to create a ticket

items.title: Sandbox, rollout and backout
items.sourceItem: User-supplied front-of-book assessment, item 47; rewritten after correction review
items.fact: Sandbox testing isolates evaluation; a backout plan explains how to reverse a failed change.
items.trap: Blackout and backout are different terms. Approval, verification and recovery planning remain part of change control.
items.transfer: Name a measurable signal that should trigger rollback in a new deployment.
items.recall: Test in a sandbox, obtain required approval and prepare a backout/rollback plan

items.title: Rename and join an AD domain
items.sourceItem: User-supplied front-of-book assessment, item 48; rewritten after correction review
items.fact: System Properties provides computer-name/domain membership controls.
items.trap: Successful domain join also requires the correct edition, network/DNS reachability and authorized credentials.
items.transfer: What would you check if the domain name cannot be resolved?
items.recall: System Properties (sysdm.cpl)

items.title: Task Manager user sessions
items.sourceItem: User-supplied front-of-book assessment, item 49; rewritten after correction review
items.fact: Task Manager’s Users view shows signed-in users and their associated activity.
items.trap: The Performance tab provides resource graphs; it answers a different question.
items.transfer: Which view would you use to examine GPU utilization rather than user sessions?
items.recall: Users

items.title: RAID 5 is supplemental Core 1 storage
items.sourceItem: User-supplied front-of-book assessment, item 50; rewritten after correction review
items.fact: Conventional RAID 5 uses distributed parity and tolerates one member failure.
items.trap: This is supplemental Core 1 storage context. Degraded/rebuild availability depends on the controller and workload; RAID is not backup.
items.transfer: What happens to redundancy after one failure, and why does a second failure threaten the array?
items.recall: RAID 5
